body:
Flaky-test detection triage for [comment 5581571760](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/pull/35831#issuecomment-5581571760), checked against `fc11c3ec0cc41173543e6b7f7b9ebdd9d545439c`:

- **J4, PerpsPositionsView.test.tsx: FALSE POSITIVE.** The proposed `await waitFor(() => {})` snippet does not exist. All 16 `waitFor` callbacks contain `expect` assertions, including the account-summary assertions at line 233 and privacy-label assertions at line 632.
- **J4, PerpsCrossMarginInfoButton.test.tsx: FALSE POSITIVE.** The file has no `waitFor` import or call. Its tests use `fireEvent` and direct modal/content assertions; there is no empty callback to replace.
- **J3, PerpsProPositionCard.test.tsx: FALSE POSITIVE.** `beforeEach` at lines 35–38 clears call history and restores `useSelector(false)`. The test-specific selector overrides are reset by that setup.
- **J3, PerpsCard.test.tsx: FALSE POSITIVE.** `beforeEach` at lines 69–93 clears calls and restores the privacy selector and market data. Those are the mock return values changed by the tests. A blanket `resetAllMocks()` would also erase the stable event-tracking factory.
- **J3, PerpsPositionCard.test.tsx: FALSE POSITIVE.** `beforeEach` at lines 206–259 clears calls and restores theme, PnL, market, price and selector behavior. Stable TP/SL and close-action hook factories are intentionally retained; blanket reset would erase their defaults.

`clearAllMocks()` does not need to be followed by `resetAllMocks()` when changed implementations are explicitly restored. These dispositions are based on the current source, not the zero historical failure rate. All ten unit-test shards pass on this commit. No code change is needed for these suggestions.

The separate typecheck failure remains the four missing `ORDER_MARGIN_MODE_*` constants from the unreleased Core change. Core #10136 is still unmerged; Mobile remains blocked until Core merge, publication, then the registry dependency update and revalidation. The lint job was cancelled.

Rebased onto `origin/main` (`9e21342485`); branch is now `9e350ce121d`, linear, no merge commit.

**The Core dependency blocker is cleared.** `main` bumped `@metamask/perps-controller` `^16.1.0` → `^16.2.0`, and the installed 16.2.0 exports all four `ORDER_MARGIN_MODE_*` constants (`perpsErrorCodes.d.cts:44-47`; its CHANGELOG credits [core#10136](https://github.com/MetaMask/core/pull/10136)). `yarn lint:tsc` now passes with zero errors, so the four TS2339 errors at `translatePerpsError.ts:77/79/81/83` are gone. No `package.json`/`yarn.lock` change is needed in this PR — main already carries the bump.

Post-rebase gate: scoped ESLint `--max-warnings=0` clean, `lint:tsc` clean, `format:check` clean, and all 5 affected suites pass (110/110 tests).

Flaky-detection findings from [comment 5581571760](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/pull/35831#issuecomment-5581571760) were re-verified independently against the rebased HEAD and the earlier dispositions hold: no empty `waitFor(() => {})` exists in either J4 file (`PerpsPositionsView` has 16 `waitFor` calls, all with assertions; `PerpsCrossMarginInfoButton` imports no `waitFor` at all), and each J3 `beforeEach` explicitly restores the mock return values its tests mutate. Adding `jest.resetAllMocks()` would additionally wipe the `jest.mock` factory implementations those suites rely on, so it would break them rather than stabilize them. No code change.

The inherited runtime recipe was not re-run to completion: it gates on exactly one real open Cross position on the testnet account, and that account currently has none (the positions used for the original validation were closed at the end of that run). The gate fails before reaching any assertion on this PR's display code, and no branch commit touches the fixture, so it is environmental rather than a regression.

- **Selected Performance tags**: None (no tests recommended)
- **Risk Level**: high
- **AI Confidence**: 100%

**E2E Test Selection:**
Hard rule (en-locale-change): locales/languages/en.json changed — UI strings and E2E text/label selectors may diverge (including platform casing like Android textAllCaps). Running all tests.

**Performance Test Selection:**
No performance-sensitive changes in this PR. All changes are UI component additions/modifications for cross margin position display, gated behind a feature flag that is disabled in production. No changes to data fetching, rendering loops, state management at scale, or other performance-critical paths. The PerpsPreps performance tag covers perps market loading and position management, but the changes here are purely UI presentation layer additions that would not meaningfully impact measured performance metrics.

</details>
